subject: Despite omitting one factor the but still it appears as NA in plot

messages.author: bd07a3cce0fa1440
messages.subject: Despite omitting one factor the but still it appears as NA in plot
parts:
Hi,
can the developers of Deducer package please take care of this bug (if
I am right). If I delete one factor in the data viewer the plot still
shows this as NA labeled. Use the mpg dataset and do boxplot as
example for reproducibility use x = drv, y=hwy. Omit the r from the
drv factor (r, f, 4) you will see the NA boxplot

messages.author: 1a09129d38549286
messages.subject: Re: Despite omitting one factor the but still it appears as NA in plot
parts:
Hi, Fadi. That's not a bug. If you create a subset of the original
data, but keep the "deleted" level in the factor, that level still
exists, and the plot just shows that fact. You have two options: (a)
drop the deleted level in the subsetted data frame before creating the
plot. (b) Modify the plot: add a "scale_x_discrete" element (tab
"Scales" in the Plot Builder), and check the box "Drop unused levels".

Helios

messages.subject: Re: Despite omitting one factor the but still it appears as NA in plot
parts:
thanks a lot Helios for the hint to option (b) that made life much easier. Deducer is really the tip of the R and ggplot2 iceberg !
option (a) is what I am used to do and I do it in the following way using our same "mgp" data:
> mpg <-mpg[mpg$drv !="r", ] # removes the factor
> mpg$drv <- factor(mpg$drv) # should be done so that dropping takes effect

regards
